title: The Vanishing Mandate
thesis: A plurality declared a mandate on election night and had no government within forty-eight hours, a contradiction that is structural rather than personal.
body:
The winner declared a mandate on election night. Two days later there was no government, no majority, and no obvious path to either [sy_dfff66e9c051, sy_37713f2aea46].

<then-now>
<then>On election night the leading party claimed a decisive mandate from a narrow plurality [sy_dfff66e9c051].</then>
<now>Within forty-eight hours coalition talks had collapsed over cabinet seats, leaving the "mandate" without a majority to enact it [sy_37713f2aea46].</now>
</then-now>

<card kind="story">[sy_37713f2aea46]</card>

<quote display="card">[qt_be9b7c8f77c0]</quote>

The contradiction is structural, not personal: a plurality is read as a mandate on the night and exposed as a negotiation by the weekend [sy_dfff66e9c051, sy_37713f2aea46].
